results.user: With my partner I do everything at home and never say when it's too much — then once every few months I explode over something tiny.
results.visibleReply:
That pattern has a particular exhaustion to it — carrying everything quietly until the container breaks, then the explosion feels disproportionate and probably makes everything worse.

Before we go further, help me understand it a bit more. When you're in the carrying-everything phase — the long stretch before the explosion — what does that feel like from the inside? Is it more like you don't notice it building, or more like you notice but push it down?

results.user: Even with my best friend — I organised her entire wedding last year while my own life was falling apart, and she never even asked how I was. I said nothing.
results.visibleReply:
Three places, same pattern. Work, home, your closest friendship — and in each one, you disappear into what's needed, say nothing about what it costs you, and eventually something gives.

What strikes me is that even when your own life was falling apart, you organised her wedding. You had access to that information — *my life is falling apart* — and still said nothing to her.

What gets in the way of saying it? When you imagine telling someone "this is too much for me" — what happens inside?

results.user: So what is wrong with me? Why do I keep doing this everywhere?
results.visibleReply:
Nothing is wrong with you. This is a pattern that makes complete sense — it developed for a reason, even if it's costing you now.

But I want to be honest with you: I don't know yet why *you* specifically do this. I have some early thoughts, but we've only just met, and I'd rather understand it properly than hand you a quick answer that might not actually fit.

What I can see clearly is the shape of it — the absorbing, the silence, the breaking. That's real and consistent across every part of your life.

The question you just asked — "why do I keep doing this" — that's exactly the right question. And to answer it well, I need to know a little more about you.

When did this start? Was there a time in your life — maybe earlier, growing up — where saying "this is too much" wasn't safe, or simply didn't work?
